audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 18, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness and reception-history audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for severe famine, Obadiah's resistance network, threatened messengers, Ahab's blame, interreligious contest, animal sacrifice, religious mockery, self-cutting, fire sign, mass execution of Baal prophets, rain, and misuse for persecution or self-harm.

verses.restored: After many days, word of YHWH came to Elijah in third year, saying, Go, show yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain upon face of ground.

familiar.text: And it came to pass after many days, that the word of the LORD came to Elijah in the third year, saying, Go, shew thyself unto Ahab; and I will send rain upon the earth.

modern.text: After a long time, in the third year of the drought, the word of the LORD came to Elijah: “Go and present yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain upon the face of the earth.”

modern.text: Then Ahab said to Obadiah, “Go throughout the land to every spring and every valley. Perhaps we will find grass to keep the horses and mules alive so that we will not have to destroy any livestock.”

verses.restored: As YHWH your Divine lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord did not send to seek you. When they said, He is not here, he made kingdom and nation swear they did not find you.

familiar.text: As the LORD thy God liveth, there is no nation or kingdom, whither my lord hath not sent to seek thee: and when they said, He is not there; he took an oath of the kingdom and nation, that they found thee not.

modern.text: As surely as the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent someone to search for you. When they said, ‘He is not here,’ he made that kingdom or nation swear that they had not found you.

verses.restored: Elijah said to prophets of Baal, Choose for yourselves one bull and prepare first, for you are many. Call upon name of your gods, but put no fire.

familiar.text: And Elijah said unto the prophets of Baal, Choose you one bullock for yourselves, and dress it first; for ye are many; and call on the name of your gods, but put no fire under.

modern.text: Then Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, “Since you are so numerous, choose for yourselves one bull and prepare it first. Then call on the name of your god, but do not light the fire.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ לִנְבִיאֵ֣י הַבַּ֗עַל בַּחֲר֨וּ לָכֶ֜ם הַפָּ֤ר הָֽאֶחָד֙ וַעֲשׂ֣וּ רִאשֹׁנָ֔ה כִּ֥י אַתֶּ֖ם הָרַבִּ֑ים וְקִרְאוּ֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖שׁ לֹ֥א תָשִֽׂימוּ

verses.restored: They took bull given them, prepared it, and called upon name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, Baal, answer us. There was no voice and no answer. They limped/danced around altar they made.

familiar.text: And they took the bullock which was given them, and they dressed it, and called on the name of Baal from morning even until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us. But there was no voice, nor any that answered. And they leaped upon the altar which was made.

modern.text: And they took the bull that was given them, prepared it, and called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, shouting, “O Baal, answer us!” But there was no sound, and no one answered as they leaped around the altar they had made.

original.text: וַ֠יִּקְחוּ אֶת הַפָּ֨ר אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֣ן לָהֶם֮ וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֒ וַיִּקְרְא֣וּ בְשֵׁם הַ֠בַּעַל מֵהַבֹּ֨קֶר וְעַד הַצָּהֳרַ֤יִם לֵאמֹר֙ הַבַּ֣עַל עֲנֵ֔נוּ וְאֵ֥ין ק֖וֹל וְאֵ֣ין עֹנֶ֑ה וַֽיְפַסְּח֔וּ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה

verses.restored: At noon Elijah mocked them and said, Call with a loud voice, for he is a god. Perhaps he is occupied, relieving himself, on a journey, or sleeping and must awaken.

familiar.text: And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked.

modern.text: At noon Elijah began to taunt them, saying, “Shout louder, for he is a god! Perhaps he is deep in thought, or occupied, or on a journey. Perhaps he is sleeping and must be awakened!”

original.text: וַיְהִ֨י בַֽצָּהֳרַ֜יִם וַיְהַתֵּ֧ל בָּהֶ֣ם אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ קִרְא֤וּ בְקוֹל גָּדוֹל֙ כִּֽי אֱלֹהִ֣ים ה֔וּא כִּ֣י שִׂ֧יחַ וְכִֽי שִׂ֛יג ל֖וֹ וְכִֽי דֶ֣רֶךְ ל֑וֹ אוּלַ֛י יָשֵׁ֥ן ה֖וּא וְיִקָֽץ

verses.restored: They called with loud voice and cut themselves according to their custom with swords and spears until blood poured upon them.

familiar.text: And they cried aloud, and cut themselves after their manner with knives and lancets, till the blood gushed out upon them.

modern.text: So they shouted louder and cut themselves with knives and lances, as was their custom, until the blood gushed over them.

verses.restored: After noon passed, they prophesied until time of grain offering. There was no voice, no answer, and no attention.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when midday was past, and they prophesied until the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice, that there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded.

modern.text: Midday passed, and they kept on raving until the time of the evening sacrifice. But there was no response; no one answered, no one paid attention.

verses.restored: Elijah said to all people, Come near to me. All people came near. He repaired altar of YHWH that was broken down.

familiar.text: And Elijah said unto all the people, Come near unto me. And all the people came near unto him. And he repaired the altar of the LORD that was broken down.

modern.text: Then Elijah said to all the people, “Come near to me.” So all the people approached him, and he repaired the altar of the LORD that had been torn down.

translation_notes: The famine is severe and collective. Ahab searches for grass to preserve royal animals while the narrative says little about hungry human communities.
Obadiah practices resistance from inside the palace, hiding and feeding one hundred threatened prophets. His fear that Ahab will kill him is credible, not cowardice.
Jezebel is responsible for a lethal persecution policy in the story, but her gender and Sidonian identity must not fuel misogyny or xenophobia. Ahab's authority and participation remain central.
The contest kills two bulls and uses scarce drought water. Religious spectacle has animal, ecological, and community costs.
Elijah's mockery of Baal and the prophets' self-cutting must not be imitated. Self-harm requires compassionate intervention, not ridicule, competition, or proof-testing.
Fire from heaven is an extraordinary narrative sign, not a safe experiment or method for determining religious truth.

Verse 40 reports the mass slaughter of 450 religious rivals. This is religious massacre and must never authorize persecution, execution, vigilantism, holy war, or violence against clergy of another tradition.
The people's acclamation after the fire occurs under intense spectacle and before mass killing; public unanimity does not make violence just.
The return of rain relieves a suffering land but does not retroactively sanctify every act Elijah performs.
Elijah's claim to be alone is later corrected by the existence of preserved faithful people. Isolation can distort perception even in a prophet.
safety_note: Maximum safeguard: Do not imitate the Carmel contest, mock or encourage self-harm, kill animals for proof, call down fire, or persecute religious rivals. The slaughter at Kishon is a massacre, not a revival method. Center Obadiah's nonviolent resistance, famine relief, compassionate care, and freedom of conscience.
